content.text:
I can't compute these percentages, because the working directory has none of the IURC order data.

The directory has only shell and editor config entries (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/*` and similar). Each of these is a character device (`/dev/null`-style, major/minor 1,3), so each reads as empty. There are no order files, PDFs, text extracts or spreadsheets covering the 58 orders. It isn't a git repository, so there's no history to recover them from. The sandbox only allows access to this directory, so I haven't looked elsewhere.

So I can't give a figure for 2021, 2024 or 2025. Any number I gave would be invented, and I won't offer one even as an estimate.

To get the answer, I need the 58 orders, or a table of their cases, placed in the working directory. The table needs the order date, case number, respondent and Abstentions field. With that I would do the following:
- Trim each Abstentions field and delete any leaked "Additional Infonnation:" or "Additional Information:" text.
- Flag a case as having a recorded abstention if any text is left.
- For 2021, 2024 and 2025, divide flagged cases by all cases in that order year and round to one decimal.
